title: Optimize your startup for growth by hiring remotely
summary: You're no longer limited to hiring within your borders. Remote hiring is here to change the game. But how to do it right? Learn the steps you need to make sure remote hiring is a success.
body_text: Running a startup in today’s world means taking advantage of every opportunity available to you. That's why embracing remote workers can be the difference between a thriving startup and one that struggles to stay afloat. According to Harvard Business Review, companies that offer remote work are 50% less likely to experience turnover. However, there are many risks associated with hiring remotely that are often not discussed or considered when making the decision to build a remote team. ‍ Today, we'll explore the tips for making it worthwhile and how to balance risk and reward when hiring remotely and find out what it takes to make the most of remote opportunities to reap major benefits for your startup. Assessment time: The Risks and Benefits ‍ ‍ Let's start with the basics...If your startup is dipping its toe into the remote work pool, you may think, “Yikes! What have I gotten myself into?” . Don't worry — it's only natural to feel a little overwhelmed when faced with the unknown. But don't let that stop you from achieving success; if your goals and objectives for taking on remote workers are properly defined, then the risk you take will be worth the reward. ‍ ‍ Let's understand some of the potential risks associated with remote work: ‍ • Communication overload – Working with a distributed team can lead to communication overload due to the sheer volume of messages coming from different channels. • Differing work ethics – Different cultures may have different work ethics, and this can be a challenge if you don't have the same standards for remote workers. • Uneven workloads – Working with a distributed team also means that some tasks may not be completed on time due to different time zones or language barriers. These are just some things to keep in mind ...are you still with me? ‍ What's Right for Your Startup? TL;DR: It is essential for startups to be able to recognize when the risk is worth taking in order to stay competitive in their market. Running a startup can be downright intimidating — especially when it comes to embracing remote work. At this point, you may be asking yourself, “Can my business really handle this?” The answer is YES! With the right strategy and team in place, you can make remote working a reality. But first, let's take a step back and ask yourself: Is this type of setup really right for my company’s culture and current goals? Checklist checkpoint: ‍ ‍ Here are some questions to consider before deciding on a remote work setup: • Is the current company culture conducive to remote work? • Are there any tasks that would be difficult or impossible to do with a remote setup? • Does everyone have access to the tools and resources they need? • What communication channels should be put in place? • How can progress and accomplishments be tracked and reported? When it comes to making a decision about hiring remotely, there are no hard-and-fast rules — sometimes the pros outweigh the cons and sometimes the opposite is true. By examining your needs carefully and doing research on what others have done successfully, you'll be able to determine if taking on remote workers is the best fit for your business. ‍ Understanding Legal Requirements & Limitations Now that you have determined remote hiring is the way to go for your startup moving forward, it's time we talk about the elephant in the room...legality. It's essential to know the legal requirements and limitations when hiring remote workers. You must ensure that your organization complies with local, state, and federal laws. Yes, I know it sounds like a headache... But when there is a will, there's a way! This is where Ontop comes in. We make it easy to hire remote workers by taking care of all the legal complexities. Take Hunty , for example, a platform that is changing how people find jobs in Latin America. They knew it was time to grow and decided to transition to hiring remotely. They had some initial concerns and met with complex bureaucracy when trying to hire in Mexico. ‍ But after getting in touch with us, they started hiring all over LATAM at a lightning fast speed . They've been able to see an overall increase in productivity while maintaining current quality standards. ‍ Bottom line: Legal requirements can seem difficult to navigate, but they don’t have to be. With Ontop on your side, you can streamline remote hiring processes and manage the legal side with ease — so you can concentrate on growing your business without having to worry about all the details. ‍ Developing a Resourceful Pool of Talent Speaking of streamlining remote hiring, it goes without saying that thinking outside of the box pays off – that’s why having a resourceful pool of talent is so important in today's business world.Not only will you beat out your competition, but you'll also have access to a diverse set of skills and perspectives that can help drive innovation. To diversify your pool of talent, remember to look beyond traditional job boards, such as LinkedIn and Indeed. Instead, consider using specialized recruiting platforms that cater to specific niches or have a track record of successful international hires.By leveraging the power of digital hiring platforms, you can access global talent quickly and cost-effectively — no matter where your company is located. ‍ Setting Up a Smart Hiring System Last but not least, you have to consider implementing an effective hiring system. This will help ensure that you make the right hiring decisions while still being mindful of budget, compliance and payroll constraints.Without the right framework and processes, it can be difficult to find qualified remote candidates and successfully manage the recruitment process from a distance. By investing in resources like applicant tracking systems or assessment tools, founders can ensure that their recruiting process follows best practices while simultaneously reducing time-to-hire.Ontop offers a comprehensive solution to help founders hire remote talent in minutes. title: First Installation of Permalok® Radial Bending Joint Completes Emergency Bypass Tunnel Project in New Jersey
body_text: 1,290 LF Curved Steel Microtunnel Utilizing Permalok® RBJ Installed by Northeast Remsco for the Emergency Pleasure Bay Interceptor Bypass Tunnel This emergency project for the Two Rivers Water Reclamation Authority (TRWRA) completes the Pleasure Bay Interceptor, originally designed as a 3,250 LF straight-run 96-inch diameter rib and lagging tunnel beneath New Jersey’s Pleasure Bay tributary to the Shrewsbury River. Approximately 70% of the tunnel had been completed when crews encountered tunnel material inflow that interrupted construction within the rib and lagging tunnel. TRWRA and project engineer Hazen and Sawyer developed an alternative approach that allowed the partially completed tunnel to be intercepted by a curved 1,290 LF microtunnel launched from the original tunnel’s exit shaft. The microtunnel was installed by Northeast Remsco using the patent-pending Permalok® RBJ (Radial Bending Joint) . This project marks the first-ever use of the RBJ technology, the only steel casing pipe designed specifically for intentionally curved microtunneling alignments. Pleasure Bay Interceptor History The Pleasure Bay Interceptor (PBI) conveys sanitary sewer wastewater from Oceanport under the bay to TRWRA’s main pump station located in Monmouth Beach. The existing PBI is a more than 50-year-old reinforced concrete pipeline, and the existing main pump station in Monmouth Beach sustained damage during Hurricane Sandy. Both are nearing the end of their service life. The newly constructed combined tunnel-microtunnel system will include a 54-inch fiberglass-reinforced polymer mortar pipe replacing the aging concrete interceptor. Emergency Bypass Project Design When the rib and lagging tunneling operation was interrupted by tunnel material inflow, TRWRA and Hazen and Sawyer evaluated numerous options to safely and effectively complete the project. The selected solution maximized the use of previously constructed infrastructure while providing the most practical and cost-effective path forward. By launching a curved microtunnel from the existing 96-foot-deep Oceanport shaft, crews could intersect the previously completed tunnel at a gentle angle, allowing successful use of both the existing tunnel infrastructure and the previously constructed tunneling exit shaft. Permalok RBJ was selected as the casing pipe because of its ability to accommodate the approximately 5,500 -foot radius curved alignment. The 72-inch OD pipe was manufactured at Northwest Pipe Company’s Permalok facility in St. Louis, MO, in 10-foot joint lengths with a 1-inch wall thickness. The shorter joint lengths provided two key advantages on the project. First, they allowed for enough joint articulation along the curved alignment for the specified bend radius to be achieved. Second, they could be handled within the extremely confined 25-foot-ID shaft, which had originally been constructed as a receiving shaft rather than a launch shaft. The curved steel microtunnel was launched from the Oceanport shaft to intersect the existing tunnel under Pleasure Bay. (Note: Conceptual graphic only and not-to-scale). Permalok RBJ Installation Converting the tunneling receiving shaft into a microtunneling launch shaft required Northeast Remsco to retrofit the structure with a concrete thrust wall capable of resisting the jacking forces generated during installation. Crews also poured a concrete working slab to provide a stable platform for the jacking frame. Despite the confined shaft and small overall project footprint, Northeast Remsco crews worked efficiently within the restricted workspace. To minimize disruption to nearby residents and maintain an accelerated installation schedule for this emergency project, crews operated around the clock in two shifts with nine crew members per shift during the 72-inch microtunnel installation portion of the project. Crews from Northeast Remsco launching the Herrenknecht AVN 1200 MTBM. The MTBM featured a retractable head that was reversed through the microtunnel and removed through the launch shaft (Photos courtesy of Northeast Remsco). Installation utilized a Herrenknecht AVN 1200 MTBM (microtunnel boring machine) skinned up to 72 inches with a retractable cutterhead, marking the contractor’s first use of this type of machine. The retractable cutterhead was necessary because the microtunnel does not terminate at a receiving shaft. Once the drive is completed, the MTBM must be retracted and removed through the launch shaft. Guidance was maintained using a VMT Total Station remote guidance system, which is the same system Northeast Remsco commonly uses on long straight microtunnel drives. Permalok RBJ pipe installs in the same way as standard Permalok press-fit joints, with no specialized tools, equipment, or field welding required. The pipe was delivered to the jobsite with internal cross bracing that helps maintain roundness during transport and staging. Onsite, crews removed the cross bracing and added specially fabricated frames designed to support internal tunnel utilities during installation. Each pipe segment was then crane-lifted into the shaft, loaded onto the jacking frame, and aligned behind the previous segment. Utilizing recommended jacking forces, crews then pushed the interlocking joint ends together, efficiently completing the connection without the need for field butt welding. Lowering and connecting a Permalok RBJ joint utilizing standard microtunneling equipment. Northeast Remsco crews completed the first several joints in approximately 20 minutes each and steadily increased their connection speed as installation progressed. To prepare for the tunnel interception, crews cut sections of the steel ribs within the existing rib and lagging tunnel, replacing them with 15 FRP ribs and 14 FRP pipe plank sections, and installed 500 psi grout within the defined tunnel intersection zone volume of approximately 70 feet. This allowed the MTBM to break through the existing tunnel wall once reached. The Permalok RBJ steel casing intersects the existing tunnel, creating a continuous bore path beneath the bay for installation of the carrier pipe. Joseph Petriello, Vice President of Trenchless Operations for Northeast Remsco Construction, discussed the contractor’s experience using Permalok: “We’ve been installing Permalok pipe for over 30 years—all diameters and sizes. The RBJ goes together the same way as the T-5 and T-7 joints. There’s a huge time savings using Permalok versus welded steel pipe. A 72-inch field weld would be approximately five hours with two men, and we can make up a Permalok joint in 15 minutes—and that’s the high end.” Securing Project Success By combining rapid collaboration, adaptive engineering, and innovative trenchless construction methods, the project team was able to recover from a major tunneling setback and successfully complete a critical wastewater crossing beneath Pleasure Bay. The success of the emergency bypass effort reflects the close coordination between TRWRA, Hazen and Sawyer, Northeast Remsco Construction, and Northwest Pipe Company’s Permalok team, along with a willingness to adopt cutting-edge technology to complete the world’s first-ever curved steel microtunnel using the Radial Bending Joint. The project also demonstrated the future potential of intentionally curved steel casing installations in complex microtunneling applications. The project used 129 pieces of 72-inch Permalok RBJ steel casing pipe, manufactured in 10-foot lengths with a 1-inch wall thickness.

body_text: View All News CleanSpark Secures Twenty-Year Lease with High-Investment Grade Global Technology Company for Data Center in Sandersville, Georgia July 14, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Twenty-year triple-net (NNN) lease totaling $6.6 billion in contracted revenue, with up to $11.6 billion after full extension options 175 MW of critical IT load with deliveries expected to begin in Q4 2027 to a high-investment-grade tenant Tenant has executed a letter of intent and exclusivity arrangement covering CleanSpark's entire Texas portfolio of 885 MW LAS VEGAS , July 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CleanSpark, Inc. (Nasdaq: CLSK) ("CleanSpark" or the "Company"), a market leading data center developer, today announced it has entered into a 20-year infrastructure lease agreement, with two five-year extension options, directly with a high-investment grade, leading global technology company at its Sandersville, Georgia, campus. The lease is expected to generate approximately $6.6 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term. Under the agreement, the global technology company will deploy production-grade infrastructure at Sandersville, dedicated to a range of computing workloads. In connection with the transaction, the tenant has also executed a letter of intent and exclusivity arrangement covering CleanSpark's entire Texas portfolio of 718 acres with up to 885 MW of secured and planned power capacity, positioning Sandersville as the first chapter of a substantially larger relationship. "This lease is a transformational moment for CleanSpark as we complete our evolution into a diversified digital infrastructure platform and begin monetizing our power portfolio at institutional scale," said Matt Schultz, CleanSpark CEO and chairman. "A 20-year commitment from a high-investment-grade global technology company with a market-leading commercial profile and exclusivity across our nearly 900 MW of additional capacity in Texas is a tremendous validation of our land-and-power strategy. We have long believed in the second-mover advantage in this sector: grow our portfolio as the market matures, then execute with excellent terms and velocity. Today's announcement validates our thesis." A Foundation Built at Sandersville The Sandersville campus was selected for its access to reliable, low-cost power, available capacity for high-density compute, and its ability to support rapid, phased deployment of advanced data center infrastructure. Since the 2022 launch of its Sandersville operations, CleanSpark has established a sustained presence in the local community, investing in energy infrastructure, site development, and long-term operations that support economic activity throughout the region. "CleanSpark has been a pillar of the Sandersville community for many years, providing job market stability, tax revenue, and broad support for what makes our part of the world special," said Mayor Jimmy Andrews. "We are excited to see CleanSpark embark on this new chapter and stand shoulder to shoulder with them to support this incredible infrastructure project." While the tenant remains confidential, they are a global technology company among the high-investment-grade cohort, facilitating CleanSpark's financing options and the multi-decade term of the lease. Transaction Details Triple net (NNN) lease with annual escalators $6.6 billion of expected contract value across the initial 20-year term $11.6 billion of expected contract value if two five-year extension options are exercised Expected cumulative NOI contribution margin of nearly 100%, or an average annual NOI contribution of approximately $330 million Estimated landlord project costs of $10-$12 million per MW of critical IT load Texas Portfolio Under Exclusivity Pursuant to the executed letter of intent, CleanSpark's entire Texas portfolio is now under exclusivity with the tenant. The Texas portfolio totals 718 acres with up to 885 MW of secured and planned power capacity, including 271 acres with nearly 300 MW at our Sealy campus and 447 acres at the Brazoria campus, where transmission-level infrastructure supports an initial 300 MW demand load with the potential to expand to 600 MW. Advisors Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC acted as financial advisor to the Company. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP acted as legal counsel to the Company. Conference Call The Company will host a conference call on Tuesday, July 14 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT to discuss the announcement. Investors can join the live webcast at clsk.news/irupdatejul26 . About CleanSpark CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK), is a market-leading data center developer with a proven track record of success. We control a portfolio of more than 1.8 GW of power, land, and data centers across the United States powered by globally competitive energy prices. Sitting at the intersection of Bitcoin , energy, operational excellence, and capital stewardship, we optimize our infrastructure to deliver superior returns to our shareholders. Monetizing low-cost, high reliability energy by producing a global emerging critical resource – compute – positions us to prosper in an ever-changing world. title: Replay Vision watches the session recordings you never will
summary: Somewhere in your session recordings is the moment a user rageclicked a dead button and walked out. There was no error thrown, and nobody filed a…
body_text: Replay Vision watches the session recordings you never will Sara Miteva Jul 31, 2026 Product updates , AI , Session replay , Self-driving Contents Somewhere in your session recordings is the moment a user rageclicked a dead button and walked out. There was no error thrown, and nobody filed a ticket – most users don't bother. They just leave. Unless you watch every session one by one, you'll never know it happened. Replay Vision , live today, is our AI layer for session recordings that finds where users are struggling. It's like a detective in your product, looking for clues on your behalf. After it finds all clues, it actually solves the mystery and sends the cracked case in the form of a PR directly to your Inbox . This is how self-driving works: once it detects a UI inconsistency, the fix is automatically drafted, and all you need to do is review and merge. Before we asked anyone to point Replay Vision at their product, we pointed it at ours. It cracked two cases in a week – same MO both times: the user saw no error, the logs pointed at the wrong suspect, and the only honest witness was the recording. Case one: the button that only looked clickable On the Web Analytics installation health tab, a line reading "Complete the PostHog installation to start seeing events" looked like the thing to click. It was plain text. The real button sat next to it under a different label and opened docs in the same tab, which unloaded the app and ended the recording, so the whole page basically played dead. A scanner reading those sessions flagged the dead click. Following the trail, it also caught the page firing a throttled refresh on every load, throwing 24,740 rate-limit errors in 30 days without ever returning fresher data, so the one thing our error tracking had plenty of was the symptom nobody was actually hitting. The fix relabeled the button, opened docs in a new tab, and stopped the refresh storm. Merged: posthog#67643 . Case two: the search that swore the event didn't exist The taxonomic filter is the picker you use to choose events and properties across insights, dashboards, and experiments. Search it for an event you know exists, and every so often it insisted: "No results." Broaden the search and the event strolled right back in, like it had somewhere to be. Two recordings about 16 hours apart caught users typing an exact event name, getting nothing, and second-guessing themselves. A 60-second cache had pinned one transient empty result and kept serving the blank, while the "No results" state showed before the real answer had landed. The fix stops caching empty results and holds the loading state until the fresh answer arrives. Merged: posthog#67499 . Neither case was cracked by a human Both PRs above reached us the same way: A scanner spotted the struggle in a recording. That finding became a signal in our Inbox . A background agent investigated it and opened a pull request. It landed in our inbox for review. We read both, and merged them. That's the self-driving loop , and Replay Vision is what plugs session recordings into it: the witness that used to need a human watching is now something the loop can act on. Point a scanner at your sessions Here's how it works: You set up a scanner, aim it at the sessions you care about, and it works one job on each, on demand, or on a schedule. Monitor – answer a yes/no question, like "did this user hit an error and quietly give up?" Scorer – rank sessions by frustration, so you watch the 10 that matter, not the 10,000 that don't. Classifier – tag what each user was trying to do. Summarizer – write up what happened in your product's words: "went through onboarding, got stuck requesting parental consent." Every observation links back to the exact moment in the recording, so you can watch the evidence before you act on it. And because scanners watch the rendered screen, they catch problems that never throw an error: spinners that never resolve, buttons that only look clickable but aren't actually clickable. Or just ask You can also ask your agents to set up your scanners for you or tell you what users are doing from Slack , PostHog Desktop , or your editor via the PostHog MCP : Set one up and see what it'll cost: Set up a scanner that flags mobile users who abandon checkout, and estimate what it'll cost me per month. Try it with PostHogAI Run one on a recording you're already looking at: Run a frustration score on this recording and tell me where it dropped. Try it with PostHogAI Read back what a scanner has already found: What are the top three issues my dead-ends scanner found on the pricing page this week? Show me an example recording for each. Try it with PostHogAI Point one at the users you're losing: Summarize the last session of every user who churned this month and give me your best guess why. Try it with PostHogAI Put one on an experiment: Create a scanner that watches my checkout experiment and tells me how users behave differently in each variant. Try it with PostHogAI Behind each one, the agent calls the Replay Vision MCP tools, drafts or runs the scanner, and reads the findings back. Open Replay Vision and put a scanner on a flow you care about. It'll watch the footage you were never going to. PostHog is the leading platform for building self-driving products. With a full suite of developer tools – AI observability , product analytics , session replay , feature flags , experiments , error tracking , logs , and more – PostHog captures all the context agents need to diagnose problems, uncover opportunities, and ship fixes. A data warehouse and CDP tie it all together, unifying that context into one source agents can read across. You can steer it all from Slack , the web app , the desktop ( PostHog Desktop ), or your own editor via the MCP . Community questions

body_text: OKLAHOMA CITY , July 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mammoth Energy Services, Inc. (NASDAQ: TUSK) ("Mammoth" or the "Company") will host a conference call on Friday, August 7, 2026, to discuss the Company's results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. The conference call will begin at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time (10:00 a.m. Central Time) . Prior to the call, the Company will issue a press release announcing its results, which will also be available in the Investor Relations section of the Mammoth website. The call will be webcast live and can be accessed through the Company's website. Participants may also join by dialing +1-201-689-8433 and requesting the Mammoth conference call . Please log in or dial in approximately 10 minutes prior to the scheduled start time. A telephonic replay will be available until August 14, 2026, by dialing +1-201-612-7415 and entering passcode 13761799# . An archived webcast will also be available shortly after the call in the Investor Relations section of the Mammoth website. Questions for management may be submitted in advance of the call by emailing TUSK@vizaraadvisors.com . About Mammoth Mammoth is an integrated, growth-oriented company providing a diversified suite of rental, infrastructure and energy services across North America. Mammoth's offerings span specialized equipment rentals supporting aviation, construction, and energy operations, as well as fiber optic engineering and construction. The Company also provides natural sand proppant for hydraulic fracturing, directional drilling services, and workforce accommodation facilities designed to support large-scale projects in remote locations. By combining technical expertise with a broad service platform, Mammoth helps customers achieve greater efficiency, flexibility and value across their operations. For more information, please visit www.mammothenergy.com . title: The Paris Saint-Germain and Yassir have signed a global partnership. The Paris Saint-Germain and Yassir have signed a global partnership
body_text: 29/06/2023 The Paris Saint-Germain and Yassir have signed a global partnership. The Paris Saint-Germain and Yassir have signed a global partnership by Yassir Share The Paris Saint-Germain and the super-app Yassir have signed a global partnership. how many times should we rest? two days? how we can test? Paris Saint-Germain and Yassir, the Super-App offering on-demand services and payments in North Africa, announce the signing of a global partnership for three seasons with the aim of developing the Yassir brand internationally. The Yassir online marketplace, offering transportation, delivery, and payment services, has chosen to partner with Paris Saint-Germain to expand its brand worldwide and strengthen its presence in the seven countries where it is already available – Algeria, South Africa, Canada, France, Morocco, Senegal, and Tunisia. For three seasons, the largest on-demand services and payment company in North Africa will benefit from unique visibility with the support of Paris Saint-Germain. Among the acquired rights, Yassir will display its name on the LED boards of the iconic Parc des Princes stadium and have the opportunity to directly address Paris Saint-Germain's 200 million followers on social media, one of the largest communities in global sports, to attract new customers through innovative campaigns. Noureddine Tayebi, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Yassir, stated: Yassir is the largest on-demand services and payment company in North Africa. In five years, we have expanded to seven countries and over fifty cities worldwide. We are confident that our alliance with Paris Saint-Germain, a French club that has become a global brand, will allow us to expand our playing field and invest in other regional, continental, and global markets. We look forward to offering our loyal customers a unique experience in the colors of Paris Saint-Germain. by Firdevs Marc Armstrong, Chief Revenue Officer of Paris Saint-Germain, said: "We are delighted to team up with a company that shares our philosophy. Yassir and Paris Saint-Germain both seek to explore new horizons, determined to push the boundaries of what is possible to continue enriching the experience of our customers and supporters." To mark this collaboration, Paris Saint-Germain and Yassir will create unique offers and experiences for the 8 million users of the Yassir Super-App worldwide, aiming to acquire and retain new users. About Paris Saint-Germain: Founded in 1970, Paris Saint-Germain is the most successful club in France and one of the top clubs in European football. Since its acquisition in 2011 by Qatar Sports Investment (QSI), the Club has achieved spectacular results on and off the field. The Club has won a national record of 11 Ligue 1 titles and 48 trophies since its creation, including an impressive 30 trophies since 2011. Paris Saint-Germain has attracted many big names over the years, including Ronaldinho, Beckham, Ibrahimovic, Messi, and currently boasts some of the world's best players. The Club has a growing community of supporters on social media, with over 200 million followers, making it one of the largest in global sports. Paris Saint-Germain is a forward-thinking club that has added an Esports team to its football, women's football, handball, and judo teams. The Club is also committed to giving back to the community and has significantly increased funding for its Foundation/Fonds de dotation, intending to develop large-scale programs for disadvantaged youth. About Yassir: Founded in 2017 by Noureddine Tayebi, Yassir is an online marketplace offering users a suite of on-demand services and payments. A comprehensive ecosystem, the Yassir Super-App provides customers with a unique solution to manage all their daily activities, from transportation to ordering groceries and meals. In addition to providing a suite of basic services, Yassir offers financial services aiming to serve the entire ecosystem, touching every component of the marketplace. Yassir is currently present in seven countries and over fifty cities in North Africa and worldwide, where it is used by over 8 million users. These services generate revenue for more than 150,000 partners. According to Forbes, Yassir ranks 5th in the Top 50 most funded startups in the MENA region. More information at https://www.yassir.com . Share
